_comment: Bigness at its limit, wherever bigness is a thing the part of the world can be -- `size` is one name
on the sun, the curtain, the bow, a feature and an island, so one word says it about all of them and
attachment decides which is meant: `colossal sun` is the star, `colossal trees features` the wood,
`colossal islands landmass` the ground, and a colossal Age is every one of them.
**The top of the axis, with `enormous` the step below it.** Two words for big are worth having only
where they do different things, so this is 1.0 and that is 0.7 upward.
It says nothing about `mingling`, and briefly did. A big landform reads as broad blotches of rock and
the implication is tempting, but binding the two made `colossal finely islands landmass` -- large
islands of finely mixed rock, an ordinary thing to want -- into two bands that cannot both be met, so
the writer was charged for a contradiction they did not make (Jonah, 2026-09-01).
The query is flat rather than keyed because `monumental` means the same thing everywhere it is
carried; a sun carries no tags at all, so asking it costs nothing and finds nothing.
